items.title: November BTO draws 37,413 applications for 7,964 flats
items.excerpt: The first BTO exercise under the higher income ceilings closed with about 4.7 applications per flat. Toa Payoh Hillside 4-room flats drew 7.0 first-timer family applications per flat, and Plantation Dew 2-room Flexi flats in Tengah drew 19.2 first-timer singles per flat. Sembawang Anchor was undersubscribed for 4-room (0.7) and 5-room (0.4) flats. An application rate shows demand, not your odds of getting a flat.

items.title: February 2027 BTO: submit HFE documents by 15 December
items.excerpt: HDB will offer about 4,300 BTO flats in Bishan, Tampines, Tengah and Toa Payoh in February 2027, alongside a Sale of Balance Flats exercise with about 5,000 flats. You need a valid HFE letter to apply, and HDB advises submitting your HFE application and all documents by 15 December 2026 so the letter is ready in time.

items.title: Toa Payoh West to get more than 6,000 new homes
items.excerpt: HDB’s master plan for Toa Payoh West adds more than 6,000 homes over the coming decade, mostly public housing. A second “heart” around Caldecott MRT station will include Toa Payoh’s first shopping mall and a 1.2-hectare wellness park. The first BTO project, Toa Payoh Hillside, was offered in November 2026. Plans like this take years, so weigh them alongside a flat’s lease, condition and recent transactions.

items.title: HDB resale prices dipped 0.1% in Q3 2026
items.excerpt: HDB’s final figures show resale prices fell 0.1% in the third quarter, slightly less than the 0.2% flash estimate and the third quarterly decline in a row. Transactions rose 19.5% to 7,645 flats. HDB has not seen a significant rise in buying by private-property owners since the 15-month wait was removed in July. For your own flat, compare similar units nearby rather than applying the headline change.

items.title: More automation planned for BTO construction from 2027
items.excerpt: HDB plans to introduce smart passenger and material hoists at about half of BTO sites tendered from 2027, and expand trials of floor-screeding robots to at least four more projects. These are planned construction improvements, rather than a change to the completion date of every existing project.

items.title: Higher income ceilings for eligible HDB buyers
items.excerpt: For HFE applications from 24 August 2026, the monthly household income ceiling rises to S$16,000 for eligible families buying a new subsidised flat, buying resale with the CPF Housing Grant, or taking an HDB loan. The corresponding ceiling for eligible singles aged 35 and above buying a subsidised flat or taking an HDB loan rises to S$8,000.

items.title: Next BTO launch moves to November 2026
items.excerpt: The next sales exercise has moved from October to November. HDB plans to offer about 7,960 flats across Bedok, Geylang, Sembawang, Tengah, Toa Payoh and Yishun, including Community Care Apartments in Toa Payoh. Buyers need a valid HFE letter when applying.

items.title: 15-month wait removed for certain private-property owners
items.excerpt: Private-property owners and former owners no longer face the 15-month wait when buying a non-subsidised HDB resale flat without an HDB loan. An HFE letter is still required. The separate 30-month wait for subsidised purchases or an HDB loan remains, so the financing route matters.

items.title: HDB resale prices fell 0.3% in Q2 2026
items.excerpt: HDB’s resale price index declined 0.3% in the second quarter, following a 0.1% fall in the first quarter. This is a market-wide measure: the price of an individual flat still depends on its location, remaining lease, condition and comparable transactions.
